key_insight: Wake-capture during plate reversal creates excess drag beyond quasi-steady predictions, and its strength is set mainly by how far the plate traveled before reversing.
engineering_relevance: For flapping-wing and reciprocating micro-air-vehicle design, controlling pre-reversal stroke length can tune unsteady force peaks and improve force prediction models.
method: Study a flat plate in forward-back translational motion at insect-flight-relevant Reynolds numbers.
Compare measured reversal-phase drag against quasi-steady estimates to isolate wake-induced excess force.
Model the starting vortex as a point vortex to explain the observed distance-dependent wake scaling.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports flow observations and force measurements showing two wake-force peaks when the starting vortex detaches and reforms, with a slower post-reversal decay for longer pre-reversal travel distances.
watch_item: The point-vortex and simplified flat-plate model captures scaling trends, but it may not transfer directly to fully 3D flapping wings or more complex wake geometries.
paper_title: Reversal of a flat plate into its wake: a minimal model for wake capture
